Terms of Reference: Integrated Travel and Expense
Management Solution

Issued by: Halcyon Ridge Holdings, Inc. (fictional), Procurement Department
Foreword
In today's rapidly evolving business landscape, organizations are increasingly recognizing the critical
importance of digital transformation as a strategic enabler of operational excellence. Halcyon Ridge Holdings,
Inc. (hereinafter referred to as "the Corporation") is committed to leveraging innovative, best-in-class
technologies to streamline its processes, enhance transparency, and empower its workforce to achieve their
full potential.
This Terms of Reference (TOR) document sets out the requirements, expectations, scope, and conditions for
the procurement of an Integrated Travel and Expense Management Solution (hereinafter referred to as "the
Solution"). The Solution is envisioned to serve as a comprehensive, end-to-end, user-centric platform that will
holistically address the travel and expense management needs of the Corporation, its business units, and its
employees.
It is important to note that this document has been prepared with the utmost care to ensure that all
requirements are clearly articulated, comprehensive, and aligned with the strategic objectives of the
Corporation. Prospective vendors are encouraged to read this document in its entirety, as requirements may
be elaborated or further described in multiple sections for clarity and emphasis.
The Corporation values partnerships that are built on trust, collaboration, and a shared commitment to
excellence. It is the Corporation's expectation that the selected vendor will not only deliver a robust and
scalable Solution but will also act as a trusted advisor throughout the engagement, bringing industry best
practices, thought leadership, and a proactive approach to problem-solving.
This TOR is organized as follows: Section 1 provides background; Section 2 states objectives; Section 3
describes the scope; Sections 4 to 6 describe functional requirements; Section 7 describes the user
experience; Section 8 covers integration; Section 9 covers business rules; Section 10 covers vendor
obligations; Sections 11 to 13 cover deliverables, warranty and evaluation.

1. Background
1.1 About the Corporation
The Corporation is a diversified holding company with operations in property development, logistics, and
consumer retail. It employs approximately 3,200 employees across a head office and 14 regional offices
nationwide. Employees travel frequently for site visits, client meetings, audits, and training activities, both
domestically and occasionally abroad.
1.2 Current situation
At present, travel and expense processes are largely manual and paper-based. Employees fill out printed
travel request forms, which are routed physically for signatures. Cash advances are requested through a
separate form and released by the Treasury unit. After travel, employees prepare expense reports in
spreadsheets, attach original paper receipts, and submit them to Finance for checking and reimbursement.
Corporate credit card statements are reconciled manually each month.
This manual process results in long processing times (an average of 18 working days from claim submission
to reimbursement), lost receipts, inconsistent application of travel policies, limited visibility for management,
and significant effort for the Finance team.
1.3 Rationale
The Corporation recognizes that a modern, integrated, and digital approach to travel and expense
management will result in significant efficiency gains, improved compliance, enhanced employee satisfaction,
and better decision-making through data-driven insights.
1.4 Contact for this TOR
All clarifications regarding this TOR shall be submitted in writing to the designated contact person.
Contact person: [NAME], Senior Procurement Officer
Email: [EMAIL]
Mobile: [MOBILE]
Clarifications received after the deadline stated in the bid timetable shall not be entertained. The Corporation
reserves the right to share responses with all prospective vendors.
Page 2 of 16

2. Objectives
2.1 General objective
The general objective of this engagement is to design, develop, test, deploy and hand over a Solution that will
digitize, automate, and optimize the end-to-end travel and expense management lifecycle of the Corporation,
from travel request to reimbursement and accounting.
2.2 Specific objectives
The specific objectives of the engagement are as follows:
1. To enable employees to submit travel requests electronically, with automatic routing to the appropriate
approvers.
2. To enable employees to request cash advances and to liquidate them within the prescribed period.
3. To enable employees to submit expense claims with digital copies of receipts.
4. To automatically check expenses against the Corporation's travel and expense policy.
5. To enable Finance to verify claims and generate reimbursement payments to employees' bank accounts.
6. To import and match corporate credit card transactions.
7. To post approved expenses to the Corporation's ERP general ledger.
8. To provide management with timely reports and dashboards.
9. To reduce the claim-to-reimbursement time from 18 working days to 5 working days or less.
2.3 Guiding principles
The Solution shall be guided by the following principles: user-centricity, simplicity, agility, scalability, security
by design, transparency, accountability, data-driven decision-making, continuous improvement, and alignment
with global best practices. The Solution shall embody a mobile-first mindset, ensuring that employees can
perform their tasks anytime, anywhere, on any device.
2.4 Expected benefits
The expected benefits include, but are not limited to: faster processing; improved policy compliance; reduced
paper usage in support of the Corporation's sustainability goals; improved employee experience; enhanced
visibility of travel spend; and stronger internal controls.
Page 3 of 16

3. Scope of work
3.1 Overview
The scope of work covers the end-to-end delivery of the Solution, including requirements validation, solution
design, development, configuration, testing, data preparation, deployment, training, documentation, and
turnover.
3.2 Functional scope summary
At a high level, the Solution shall cover the following functional areas, which are further detailed in Sections 4
to 9:
- Travel requests, including destination, travel dates, purpose and estimated cost.
- Approval of travel requests and expense claims by the appropriate approvers.
- Cash advance requests and their liquidation.
- Expense claims with receipt images.
- Automatic reading of receipts to reduce manual encoding.
- Policy compliance checks, including per-diem limits.
- Finance verification of claims.
- Reimbursement through bank payment files.
- Corporate credit card transaction matching.
- Posting of journal entries to the ERP general ledger.
- Notifications and reminders.
- Reports and management dashboards.
- Maintenance of cost centers, expense categories, per-diem rates, and organization hierarchy.
- Audit trail.
3.3 User groups
The Solution shall serve the following user groups:
- Employees (approximately 3,200), who request travel, cash advances and reimbursements.
- Approvers (immediate supervisors, department heads and senior management), who review and approve
requests.
- Finance staff (approximately 25), who verify claims, process reimbursements and reconcile card
transactions.
- Treasury staff (approximately 6), who release cash advances.
- System administrators (2), who maintain reference data and configuration.
- Management, who monitor travel spend through reports and dashboards.
3.4 Exclusions from scope
Airline, hotel and travel agency fees, as well as corporate card and bank charges, are borne by the
Corporation and are not part of the vendor's price.
Page 4 of 16

4. Functional requirements
4.1 Travel request
The Solution shall allow employees to create and submit travel requests. Each travel request shall capture, at
a minimum, the following information: traveler, destination (city and country), travel dates, purpose of travel,
mode of transport, accommodation requirements, and estimated cost broken down by category (transport,
lodging, meals, incidentals). The employee shall be able to save a travel request as a draft and submit it later.
The Solution shall validate that the travel dates are in the future and that the estimated cost is provided for
each category.
Upon submission, the travel request shall be routed automatically to the approvers in accordance with the
approval workflow described in Section 4.2. The employee shall be able to view the status of the request at
any time.
The Solution shall allow employees to cancel a travel request that has not yet been fully approved. Cancelled
requests shall be retained for reference and audit purposes.
4.2 Approval workflow
The Solution shall provide an approval workflow for travel requests, cash advance requests and expense
claims. Approvals shall follow a two-level approval process: the employee's immediate supervisor shall
approve first, followed by the department head as the final approver.
Each approver shall be able to approve, reject, or return the request for revision, with remarks. Rejections and
returns shall require remarks. The Solution shall notify the requester of every approval action.
Approvers who are on leave shall be able to delegate their approval authority to another employee for a
defined period. The Solution shall record that an approval was made by a delegate on behalf of the original
approver.
The approval workflow shall be efficient, transparent and auditable, ensuring that requests do not remain
pending unnecessarily. Requests pending for more than three working days with an approver shall be
escalated to the next approver.
Page 5 of 16

4.3 Cash advance
Employees with an approved travel request shall be able to request a cash advance of up to 80% of the
approved estimated cost. Cash advance requests shall follow the approval workflow. Once approved, the
Treasury unit shall record the release of the cash advance, including the release date and the mode of
release.
After travel, the employee shall liquidate the cash advance by submitting an expense claim linked to the
advance. The Solution shall compute the difference between the advance and the actual expenses, showing
either an amount to be returned by the employee or an additional amount to be reimbursed. Cash advances
not liquidated within 10 working days after the end of travel shall be flagged as overdue.
4.4 Expense claim
The Solution shall allow employees to submit expense claims, with or without a prior travel request. Each
claim shall consist of one or more expense lines. Each line shall capture the date, expense category, amount,
currency, merchant, cost center and a description. Each line shall require an image or PDF of the receipt,
except for categories designated by Finance as not requiring receipts (for example, per-diem allowances).
The Solution shall support foreign currency expenses and shall convert them to Philippine pesos using the
exchange rate on the expense date, as maintained by Finance.
Expense claims shall follow the approval workflow and shall then be verified by Finance (Section 4.7).
4.5 Automatic reading of receipts
To reduce manual encoding and improve the employee experience, the Solution shall read uploaded receipt
images and automatically extract the merchant name, date, total amount, and tax amount to prefill the
expense line. The employee shall be able to correct any extracted value before submitting. The Solution shall
indicate which values were extracted automatically.
The vendor shall propose the receipt-reading technology to be used and shall state the expected extraction
accuracy for typical Philippine receipts.
Page 6 of 16

4.6 Policy compliance checks
The Solution shall automatically check each expense line against the Corporation's travel and expense policy.
Policy rules include, but are not limited to:
- per-diem limits for meals and lodging, which vary by destination city and by employee grade;
- maximum amounts per expense category;
- categories requiring prior approval;
- duplicate receipts (same merchant, date and amount).
Expense lines that violate a policy rule shall be flagged with the reason. The employee shall provide a
justification for each flagged line before submitting. Approvers and Finance shall see the flags and
justifications.
4.7 Finance verification
After approval, Finance staff shall verify each expense claim against the receipts and the policy. Finance shall
be able to approve the claim for payment, adjust an expense line with a reason, or return the claim to the
employee. Finance shall be able to select a sample of claims for detailed audit based on amount or flag count.
4.8 Reimbursement
The Solution shall group claims approved for payment into reimbursement batches and generate a bank
payment file in the format required by the Corporation's payroll bank, crediting each employee's payroll
account. Batches shall be numbered and shall not be regenerated once released. The Solution shall record
the payment date of each claim upon confirmation by Finance.
The Corporation will provide the bank's file specification during the project.
Page 7 of 16

4.9 Corporate credit card transactions
Selected employees hold corporate credit cards. The Solution shall import the monthly card transaction file
from the issuing bank and match each transaction to expense lines submitted by the cardholder. Unmatched
transactions shall be listed for the cardholder to explain or claim. Personal transactions shall be identified by
the cardholder and deducted through payroll.
4.10 ERP posting
Upon payment, the Solution shall generate journal entries for approved expenses, charging the appropriate
cost centers and general ledger accounts, and shall post them to the Corporation's ERP. The vendor shall
implement the interface using the ERP's available interface methods. Posting errors shall be reported to
Finance for correction and reposting.
4.11 Notifications and reminders
The Solution shall send email notifications to users for relevant events, including submission, approval,
rejection, return, escalation, release of cash advance, and payment. The Solution shall send reminders to
employees with cash advances due for liquidation, and to approvers with pending items.
4.12 Travel needs
The Solution shall seamlessly handle all travel-related needs of employees in an optimal manner, ensuring a
world-class experience throughout the travel journey and leveraging the latest innovations as appropriate.
Page 8 of 16

5. Reports and dashboards
5.1 Reports
The Solution shall provide standard reports, including but not limited to: travel spend by department, cost
center and expense category; cash advances outstanding and overdue; claims by status and processing time;
policy violations by department; and corporate card transactions unmatched. Reports shall be filterable by
period and organization unit and exportable to Excel.
5.2 Management dashboard
The Solution shall provide a dashboard for management showing total travel spend versus budget, top
spending departments, average claim processing time against the 5-working-day target, policy compliance
rate, and outstanding cash advances. The dashboard shall allow drill-down from organization level to
department and cost center.
6. Administration
6.1 Reference data
System administrators shall maintain cost centers, expense categories (including whether a receipt is required
and the GL account mapping), per-diem rates per city and employee grade, exchange rates, and policy limits.
Changes shall have effective dates.
6.2 Organization hierarchy and approvers
System administrators shall maintain the organization hierarchy (company, business unit, department) and
each employee's immediate supervisor and department head, which drive approval routing. Delegations shall
be visible and editable by administrators.
6.3 Audit trail
The Solution shall maintain a complete audit trail of all transactions, recording who did what and when,
including the before and after values of changed data. Authorized users shall be able to search and export the
audit trail.
Page 9 of 16

7. User experience
7.1 Personal workspace
Each employee shall have a personal workspace showing "My Requests", "My Cash Advances", "My Claims"
and "My Card Transactions", with the status of each item. Approvers shall see "For My Approval" with pending
items and their age. Finance staff shall see the verification queue and reimbursement batches. The Solution
shall show each user only the information appropriate to their role.
The Solution shall provide a modern, intuitive, and visually appealing interface that requires minimal training,
consistent with contemporary consumer applications.
7.2 Travel request experience
As described in Section 4.1, employees shall be able to create travel requests specifying destination, dates,
purpose, and estimated costs, save drafts, and submit them for approval. The employee shall be able to track
the request status in their personal workspace.
7.3 Expense claim experience
As stated in Section 4.4, employees shall be able to submit expense claims by adding expense lines and
attaching photos of receipts taken with their mobile phone camera directly from the browser. The Solution
shall make the process quick and convenient, so that an employee can submit a typical claim in under five
minutes.
7.4 Cash advance experience
Employees shall be able to request cash advances against approved travel and liquidate them after travel, as
stated in Section 4.3, and shall see the amount due to or from them.
7.5 Reminders
The Solution shall remind employees by email about cash advances nearing the liquidation deadline and shall
remind approvers of items waiting for their action.
Page 10 of 16

7.6 Complete history
To promote transparency and enable employees and managers to understand spending patterns, each
employee shall be able to view their complete history of travel requests, cash advances and expense claims
since January 2019 in their personal workspace, and managers shall be able to view the history of their team
members for the same period.
8. Integration and interoperability
8.1 General
The Solution shall be interoperable with the Corporation's existing and future systems, adopting open
standards and modern integration patterns. The Solution shall expose well-documented interfaces where
appropriate and shall be designed to accommodate future integrations without major rework.
8.2 ERP integration
As described in Section 4.10, the Solution shall post journal entries for approved and paid expenses to the
Corporation's ERP general ledger, with the correct cost center and GL account per expense category. The
interface shall handle posting errors gracefully, allow reposting after correction, and provide a log of all
postings.
8.3 Bank files
As described in Sections 4.8 and 4.9, the Solution shall generate reimbursement payment files for the payroll
bank and shall import corporate card transaction files from the card-issuing bank, in the formats specified by
the respective banks.
8.4 Email
The Solution shall send emails through the Corporation's email service.
Page 11 of 16

9. Business rules
9.1 General
The business rules described in this section shall be configurable where possible and shall be applied
consistently across all business units.
9.2 Filing deadlines
Expense claims shall be filed within 30 calendar days after the expense date. Claims filed beyond this period
shall require the approval of the department head with justification.
9.3 Approval levels
All travel requests, cash advances and expense claims shall be subject to a three-level approval process: (1)
immediate supervisor; (2) department head; and (3) the Chief Financial Officer for requests with a total
amount above PHP 50,000. Requests at or below PHP 50,000 shall be final upon approval by the department
head. The approval routing shall be based on the organization hierarchy maintained in the Solution, and
approvers may delegate their authority during leave.
9.4 Per-diem and policy limits
As stated in Section 4.6, per-diem allowances for meals and lodging depend on the destination city and the
employee's grade. The rates shall be maintained by Finance with effective dates. Expenses exceeding the
applicable limits shall be flagged and shall require justification from the employee.
9.5 Currency
All amounts shall be stored in the original currency and in Philippine pesos.
Page 12 of 16

10. Non-functional requirements
10.1 General quality attributes
The Solution shall be secure, reliable, scalable, highly available, performant, maintainable, user-friendly, and
compliant with all applicable laws, regulations, and standards. The Solution shall adopt industry best practices
in software engineering, information security, and data protection.
The Solution shall be available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with minimal downtime. The Solution shall be
able to handle the current and future number of users and transactions of the Corporation without degradation
in performance. The Solution shall respond quickly to user actions.
The Solution shall protect personal information in accordance with the Data Privacy Act of 2012 and its
implementing rules and regulations, as well as the Corporation's data privacy policies.

The Solution shall be designed with future-proofing in mind, enabling the Corporation to adapt to changing
business needs and emerging technologies. The Solution shall support continuous improvement and
innovation.
10.2 Security
The Solution shall implement appropriate security controls to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and
availability of data. All data shall be encrypted in transit and at rest. The vendor shall follow secure coding
practices.
10.3 Usability
The Solution shall be intuitive and easy to use, requiring minimal training. The Solution shall be accessible
from desktop and mobile browsers.
Page 13 of 16

11. Vendor obligations
11.1 Project management
The vendor shall assign a dedicated project manager and a competent project team. The vendor shall conduct
regular status meetings, submit weekly status reports, and maintain a risk and issue log throughout the
engagement.
11.2 Methodology
The vendor shall adopt an agile delivery methodology with iterative releases, enabling the Corporation to
provide feedback early and often. Each iteration shall end with a demonstration of working software.
11.3 Training
The vendor shall conduct train-the-trainer sessions for key users from Finance, Treasury and system
administration, and shall provide user guides and short video tutorials for employees and approvers.
11.4 Equipment
The vendor shall supply forty (40) laptop computers with standard office software for the Finance staff who will
process claims in the Solution, delivered and configured before user acceptance testing.
11.5 Documentation
The vendor shall provide complete documentation, including solution architecture, technical design, interface
specifications, deployment guide, operations manual, and source code with build instructions.
11.6 Knowledge transfer
The vendor shall conduct knowledge transfer sessions for the Corporation's IT team covering the architecture,
configuration, deployment and support of the Solution.
Page 14 of 16

12. Deliverables and timeline
12.1 Deliverables
1. Inception report with detailed work plan.
2. Validated requirements and solution design.
3. Working software increments every two weeks.
4. Test plans and test results.
5. Deployed Solution in the production environment.
6. Training materials and completed training.
7. Documentation and source code.
8. Project closure report.
12.2 Timeline
The Corporation expects the Solution to be in production within eight (8) months from the issuance of the
notice to proceed, including user acceptance testing.
12.3 Acceptance
Each deliverable shall be subject to review and acceptance by the Corporation. The Corporation shall provide
feedback within ten working days.
13. Warranty and support
The vendor shall provide a warranty period of twelve (12) months after go-live, during which defects shall be
corrected at no additional cost. The vendor shall provide technical support with response times appropriate to
the severity of the issue.
Page 15 of 16

14. Evaluation
14.1 Evaluation criteria
Proposals shall be evaluated based on technical merit (60%) and financial proposal (40%). Technical merit
includes understanding of requirements, proposed solution, methodology, team qualifications, and relevant
experience.
14.2 Closing
The Corporation looks forward to receiving proposals from qualified vendors who share its vision of a digital,
efficient and employee-centric travel and expense management process. The Corporation reserves the right
to accept or reject any or all proposals, to waive minor deficiencies, and to award the contract to the proposal
most advantageous to the Corporation.
Annex A: Glossary
- Cash advance: an amount released to an employee before travel, to be liquidated after travel.
- Liquidation: the submission of actual expenses against a cash advance.
- Per diem: a daily allowance for meals and incidental expenses during travel.
- Cost center: an organizational unit to which costs are charged.
- GL account: a general ledger account in the ERP.

features.name: Travel Request CRUD and Workflow
features.description: Employees can create, save drafts, submit, view status, and cancel travel requests capturing traveler, destination, dates, purpose, transport mode, accommodation, and estimated costs by category. Travel dates must be future dates and estimated costs validated. Travel requests are routed automatically to approvers following a configurable approval workflow with two or three levels depending on amount thresholds. Approvers can approve, reject or return with remarks. Delegation of approval authority is supported. Requests pending more than 3 working days are escalated. Cancelled requests are retained for audit.
features.route_reason: Feature describes standard travel request and approval workflow with clear actors and outcomes.
features.justification: N-level approval workflow pattern with 2-3 levels, delegation, SLA escalation, and complex validations
acceptance_criteria: Given a travel request with future travel dates and estimated costs by category, When submitted, Then it is routed automatically to approvers per configurable workflow.
Given a travel request pending approval for more than 3 working days, When SLA expires, Then the request escalates to the next approver and notifications are sent.
Given an approver on leave with delegation active, When the delegate approves, Then the approval is recorded as on behalf of the original approver.
Given a travel request, When cancelled before full approval, Then it is retained for audit and no further approval actions occur.
